entries.title: Addon API Kit
entries.snippet: AddonAPIKit Expose APIs from your Minecraft Bedrock addons so other addons can call into them. AddonAPIKit builds on MCBE-IPC to provide a typed, request-response API layer over Minecraft's script event system. One addon defines named endpoints with typed parameters and return values; any other addon can call those endpoints…

entries.title: Calling An API
entries.snippet: Calling an API AddonAPICaller lets your addon call endpoints exposed by another addon. Before the first call to a given server, it contacts that server to fetch its list of valid endpoints and caches them locally. This means you get a clear error if you reference an endpoint that does not exist, rather than a silent failure.

entries.title: Creating A Caller
entries.snippet: Creating a caller Create one AddonAPICaller instance per API server you want to call. Pass the server name and the API version you expect to target: import { AddonAPICaller } from './AddonAPIKit.js'; const playerInfoAPICaller = new AddonAPICaller('playerInfo', '1.0.0'); The name must match the server name the publishing addon…

entries.snippet: Creating a server A server is the entry point for your addon's API. Give it a name and a version. entries.title: Manual
entries.snippet: Manual Download AddonAPIKit.js from the releases page and copy it into your addon's script directory. Import from it directly.

entries.title: Publishing An API
entries.snippet: Publishing an API AddonAPIKit lets you expose named endpoints from your addon so other addons can call into your code. You define what data each endpoint accepts and returns using PROTO models, and the library handles serialization, routing, and error handling over Minecraft's script event system.

entries.title: Models
entries.snippet: Models AddonAPIKit uses PROTO models from MCBE-IPC to define the types of data your endpoints accept and return. Because Minecraft's script event system carries everything as a string, PROTO serializes your typed values to binary and encodes them for transport. Models describe the shape of that data so the server and caller a…

entries.title: Simple Primitive
entries.snippet: Simple primitive If an endpoint returns or receives a single primitive value, use the type directly: import { PROTO } from './AddonAPIKit.js'; const CountModel = PROTO.Int32;

entries.snippet: VoidModel VoidModel is used to send or receive nothing. import { VoidModel } from './AddonAPIKit.js'; Use it as the parameter model when an endpoint takes no input, or as the return model when an endpoint has no meaningful return value. entries.title: Nested Model
entries.snippet: Nested model Models compose freely. This defines an object whose members field is an array of strings: const TeamModel = PROTO.Object({ name: PROTO.String, members: PROTO.Array(PROTO.String) });

entries.title: Object With Multiple Fields
entries.snippet: Object with multiple fields Use PROTO.Object when you need to pass or return a structured value: const PlayerModel = PROTO.Object({ name: PROTO.String, health: PROTO.Float32, level: PROTO.Int32 });

entries.title: Object With Optional Fields
entries.snippet: Object with optional fields Wrap a field in PROTO.Optional when it may not be present. The receiving end will see either the value or undefined : const PlayerModel = PROTO.Object({ name: PROTO.String, team: PROTO.Optional(PROTO.String) });
